learningObjective: Identify scenarios where INT8 GEMM is NOT faster than FP16 GEMM on an Ampere-class GPU.
profileData:
On A100 (Tensor Core INT8 peak ~ 2× FP16 peak):
  Case 1: M=4096, N=4096, K=4096, batched=1. INT8 GEMM ≈ 0.5× FP16 GEMM runtime (compute-bound; INT8 wins).
  Case 2: M=1, N=4096, K=4096 (GEMV / decode batch=1). INT8 kernel time ≈ FP16 kernel time (bandwidth-bound; weights dominate).
stem: On A100, INT8 GEMM has ~2× the FP16 Tensor Core throughput, yet Case 2 (M=1) shows INT8 no faster than FP16. What is the correct explanation?

options.text: The M=1 case has such low arithmetic intensity that CUDA cannot launch a grid at all; the runtimes reflect kernel-launch overhead only.
INT8 Tensor Cores are disabled on A100 in cuBLAS; the observed times are FP16 in both cases.

At M=1 (batch-1 decode), the kernel is bandwidth-bound: the dominant cost is loading the K×N weight matrix, which is the same size regardless of activation dtype. INT8 activations barely affect memory traffic when they represent a tiny fraction of the total bytes moved; peak-TOPS advantage of INT8 Tensor Cores cannot be realized because there is not enough compute per byte.
INT8 GEMM at M=1 is slower than FP16 due to quantize/dequantize overhead in the kernel; the fix is to disable dequantization.

explanation: At M=1 with FP16 weights (K*N = 4096*4096 = 16 MB), the kernel is bandwidth-bound; the FP16 activation vector is negligible. Replacing FP16 activations with INT8 activations saves at most K bytes; the weight matrix bytes dominate. Since both kernels move the same weight bytes (both FP16 weights in this case), the INT8 kernel's TC advantage cannot manifest — the compute path is idle waiting on weight loads. The proper solution is weight-only quantization (W4A16, W8A16) that reduces the weight bandwidth. Options B, C, D are inventions.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: CUDA can launch any grid; kernel-launch overhead is not the story here.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: INT8 Tensor Cores are enabled on A100 in cuBLAS.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: bandwidth-bound M=1 case where compute peak is irrelevant.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: quantize/dequantize overhead is minor; the primary issue is weight bandwidth.

assumptions: Both configurations use FP16 weight storage.
GPU has sufficient memory bandwidth headroom for FP16 weights but not compute-bound at M=1.
nonImplications: Does not imply INT8 GEMM is useless — for compute-bound (large M) cases it delivers.
Does not imply W4A16 solves all bandwidth issues — for very small K it may not.

sourceRefs.locator: Bandwidth vs. compute analysis for W4A16 vs W8A8

performanceClaim.scope: INT8 vs FP16 GEMM at M=1 (batch-1 decode) on A100
